127:## Drafting With Agent
128-
129-Several stories can be drafted at once, each in a run of its own. "Draft with agent" is an item of the menu of every card in Draft, the Backlog, and Next sprint, the menu its hover button opens and right-clicking opens at the pointer, as the parts say, and a button of the bulk bar, drafting every selected story; a card in Current sprint or Done, and a finding, has no such item. It is meant mainly for Draft's rough stories, but drafts any story it is offered on.
130-Each story drafts as "Ask agent" drafts an open story, with no request box and nothing to type: the run is told the story's title, its prompt, its mode, and its steps, and asked to turn it into a full story, a fuller prompt, the mode that fits it, the steps it needs, and its spec citations, grounded as the spec grounding says; and, where the story holds more than one piece of work, to split it, as drafting says: the story's rewrite, the first piece, with its steps, then a "New story" proposal for each other piece, each with its own title, prompt, mode, and spec citations, grounded the same way. A story that is one piece of work gets only its rewrite and its steps. Each run is its own, in a run of its own with no session, a Question run as the proposals say, with the planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts). All the runs start at once, none waiting on another, however many stories are drafted; one ending, failing, or being stopped never touches the others. A story already drafting is skipped, so drafting it again starts no second run.
131-The drafts never take over the side panel, which holds only one thing at a time, as the layout says: a story drafting this way shows its run on its own card, and opening the story while it drafts shows the story in the panel as ever, its run going on. While its run goes, the card's property row shows the loading state, as the states say, "Drafting…" with its spinner, in place of its status, and its menu has "Stop", which stops that run alone and keeps whatever it had proposed by then, in place of "Draft with agent". A run that fails shows its error on that card, beneath its property row, as the states say, in the theme's error colour with "Details" collapsed and "Try again", which drafts the story again; the error stays until the story is drafted again or opened. A run cut off when the application quits, as every run is, shows the same error once it is open again.
132-When a run ends, its card's property row shows how many of its proposals are waiting, as "3 proposals", in the theme's accent, or "1 proposal", counting down as each is decided and gone once none is left, counting every kind: its rewrite, its additions, and its new stories; a run that proposed nothing shows "Nothing proposed", muted, until the story is next opened. Opening the story shows them all in the side panel, beneath the story's own fields, under a "Proposals" heading, as proposal cards, as the proposal cards say, each new story's card labelled "New story", in the order the run gave them, its rewrite first, then its new stories and additions in the order given, with "Accept all" and "Reject all" beneath the last; "Accept all" accepts the rewrite, every addition, and every new story together. Drafting a story again while proposals of its wait adds the new ones after them.
133-A story's waiting proposals are kept until each is decided, saved with the plan as soon as its run ends, in `.suspense/planning/proposals/`, a file per story named by its id, so they come back, and its card's count with them, after closing Planning, a reload, or a restart. A story deleted takes its waiting proposals with it, and one duplicated copies none.
134-Nothing reaches the plan until it is accepted, as the proposals say. Accepting the story's rewrite rewrites it as proposed, and accepting an addition adds its step to the story's end, as the proposal cards say. Accepting a new story split off it adds that story at the end of the Backlog, marked "From agent", as the proposal cards say, never into Draft and never into Next sprint. A story in Draft whose rewrite or addition is accepted moves to the end of the Backlog, as "Move to backlog" moves it and motion animates it, staying open if it was; accepting a new story split off it never moves it, and a story in the Backlog or Next sprint stays where it is. A story sent while its proposals waited can no longer be rewritten or added to, as the proposal cards say.
135-
136-## Proposals
137-
138-The agent never writes the plan itself. Its run is a Question run, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox) says, able to read the project and change nothing, and Suspense data is never granted to it, so it can't touch `.suspense/planning/`; it only proposes, and nothing it proposes reaches the plan until the user accepts it.
139-Each proposal is one concrete task, with a title, a prompt, and the mode that fits it, and says where it should go: either "New story", to become a story of its own, or "Add to" a story, naming an existing story the run was shown, the open story first, to be added to it, or, in a draft about a story, "Rewrite", the story itself rewritten, as drafting says. The planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts) asks for each proposal as a fenced block whose info string is `suspense-story`, holding its title, its mode, its target, `new`, the story's id, or `rewrite`, its `spec` list of citations into the Piton source, as the spec grounding says, and its prompt, so the application reads it whatever else the reply says. The planning prompt explains the form with an example, as:
140-```suspense-story
141-title: Close a finished sprint
142-mode: chain
143-target: new
144-spec:
145-- spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint: when Close sprint shows
146-- No match: archiving a closed sprint
147-prompt:
148-Close sprint is offered once every story of the current sprint has
149-ended, as spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint says.
150-```
151-A block that names a story that no longer exists is shown as "New story", with a muted note saying so.
152-
153-## Spec Grounding
154-
155-A drafted story is grounded in the project's spec, never written from the request alone. Before proposing, the drafter searches the spec for what each story touches: the requirements and behaviours it changes or relies on, the names it uses, as a feature, a component, or a property, and the sections they are in. It reads the spec as every run does, from its compiled reference or from what `piton slice` prints, never from the Piton source, as the [ModeSystemPrompts](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts) says, and the planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts) tells it to.
156-Each proposal cites what it found, specifically: its `suspense-story` block holds a `spec` list, one entry per element, each a link to the element in the spec's Piton source, under the spec location, never to the compiled reference: the .pi file, relative to the project directory, then `#` and the element it names, an anchor or a property on one, in the form `piton slice` takes, as `spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint`, with a short line of what in it the story touches. The story's prompt names those elements and links to them in the same form. Only elements the drafter found are cited, and where they point is the only thing that is Piton source: the drafter still learns what the spec says only from the compiled reference or from what `piton slice` prints, never by reading the Piton source, as the [ModeSystemPrompts](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts) says, and works out each element's source from what `piton slice` prints for it, which names the file each declaration is in.
157-The application checks each link against the Piton source when the proposal arrives: the file has to exist under the spec location, and has to define the named element, the anchor declared in it and, for a property, that property on it, as `piton slice` would find it. A link that fails either check is dropped, with a muted note on the card saying which link it dropped and why, "no such file" or "the file doesn't define Planning.sprint". Each citation, on the proposal card and in an accepted story's "Spec" list, opens that place in the Piton source, the file in the editor at the element's declaration, as the [OpenFile](../open-file/index.md#open-file) opens a file.

// The prompt for Planning's drafting, asking the harness to propose
// stories grounded in the project's spec, never to write the plan: the
// request, how to search the spec, the stories in the plan, the story asked
// about where there is one, the reply asked for, then what is wanted under
// its heading. Drafting one story with the agent asks for what `story` says
// in place of a request typed. <reference> is filled in with where the compiled reference
// is, and <spec> with the spec location, which citations point into.

export anchor Planning:
    request:
        Below is what someone wants done in their project, in their own words.
        Propose the concrete tasks it needs: pieces of work each sent to a
        coding agent on its own, in the order they should be done, few and
        whole, one for each thing they would check off. Read the project as
        you need to, but change nothing: you only propose, and the person
        decides what goes into their plan. Each proposal says where it goes:
        a new story of its own, or added to one of the stories listed below,
        as a further step of it. Give each a short title, a prompt saying
        what should be true once it is done, in their own terms, and the mode
        it is sent in: chain to change the spec and then the code to match
        it, code to change only the code, spec to change only the spec, ask
        for a question that changes nothing, or freeform to pass the prompt
        to the agent as it is written. Prefer chain for new behaviour.

    grounding:
        A story is never written from the request alone. Before proposing,
        search the project's spec for what each story touches: the
        requirements and behaviours it changes or relies on, the names it
        uses, as a feature, a component, or a property, and the sections they
        are in. Read the spec from its compiled reference, the Markdown under
        <reference>, or from what piton slice prints for one thing, never
        from the Piton source. Cite only what you found: each citation is a
        link to the element in the spec's Piton source, under <spec>: the .pi
        file, relative to the project directory, then # and the anchor or the
        property on one it names, in the form piton slice takes, as
        <spec>/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint. Work out each
        element's file from what piton slice prints for it, which names the
        file each declaration is in, and never read the Piton source to learn
        what it says. Begin each citation with what kind of element it is,
        Requirement, Behaviour, Name, or Section, then the link, then a short
        line of what in it the story touches, then, in double quotes, the few
        words of the spec it rests on. The story's prompt names those
        elements and links to them in the same form, so the run it is sent
        to reads them first. Where nothing in the spec matches part of a
        story, never make one up: give an entry reading No match, with what
        you looked for, and say plainly in the prompt that the spec has
        nothing on it yet, so the change is new.

    stories: The stories in the plan, by id, that can be added to

    about: The story this is about, which proposals should add to where they belong to it

    story:
        Turn the story above into a full story, ready to be sent. It may be
        only a rough note: a title, or a line or two. Propose its rewrite,
        with target rewrite: a short title, a fuller prompt saying what
        should be true once it is done, the mode that fits it, and its spec
        citations. Then propose each further step it needs, in order, each
        a block of its own whose target is the story's id, a piece of the
        story done after the one before. Propose no step it already has.

    reply:
        Give each proposal as a fenced code block whose info string is
        suspense-story, holding a line each for its title, its mode, and its
        target, new for a new story, the id of the story to add to, or
        rewrite to rewrite the story this is about in place, then a
        spec line followed by its citations, one per line, each begun with a
        dash, then a blank line and its prompt, as this one is:

    wanted: What is wanted
